summary: drafted six units for the four issue-3 proposals: two new nodes (backfill workflow, resume) plus additive revisions to spec-gate, spec-producer, conductor and workflows

detail: round 1 blocked on five findings. The load-bearing one: the corroboration stage's applicability was file-granular while its scope was diff-granular, so the stage would have blocked its own CR and the first CR to touch any of 37 corpus nodes carrying no extensions field. Re-derived to hunk granularity across all three artifact-read tells. The step-record tell was a fourth list keyed to a bar that did not exist and checking entry count rather than correspondence; re-derived as a correspondence check against the drawn graph, the map and the use cases, bound to a declarable bar. A generic per-step decision node was drawn for a rule with one real instance, making the (path class, edge) pair ill-defined for two scenarios; cut it and drew step 3's real three-way branch instead. One extensions row claimed a divergence the graph could not take; dropped as a co-owned seam owned by remediation-governance. The resume node asserted a per-segment attribution its own prose said did not exist; re-derived to the observable case, a smaller inherited set.

round 2 found two regressions against artifacts round 1's remediation changed. The severe one is self-inflicted: the edit that redrew the backfill CFG matched its section heading where the string also occurs inside the steps table, truncating the node from that point and destroying its Use Cases, Control Flow and Scenario map. The node's own rule then applies to its repair - rewrite whole from the CFG, not patch. The second: narrowing the tell's applicability from file to row did not stop the stage blocking its own CR, because this CR edits a use-case row in a node that states no extensions anywhere.

why.blast: medium - the SDD self-spec's authoring and gate nodes
why.novelty: medium - two design forks the judge ruled a third remediation round cannot settle by editing
why.confidence: low - two of round 2's four findings are regressions against round 1's own remediation, so the loop is not converging and the doctrine stops it for a re-plan

detail: post-re-plan round: oracle and builder passed, architect failed on two. The load-bearing one is that the rewritten backfill graph routed every re-derivation through step one unconditionally, which encodes re-run-from-the-top - the exact behavior the node exists to forbid, and stated twice in its own prose. Redrawn as a decision over the earliest implicated step with both arms mapped, and a negative scenario added asserting steps before the re-entry point keep their entries. Also removed a dangling bar identifier for a governance that does not exist (the tell fires on the relayed mode, so it needs no registry entry), corrected a measured count that was off by one inside the rationale of a stage whose thesis is check-the-artifact-not-the-claim, and named two residual escapes rather than leaving them implied. Provenance: these are findings against content this round's re-plan authored, not against a prior remediation round's fix; the loop is converging - oracle and builder went FAIL, FAIL, PASS and the architect findings narrowed from the stage blocking its own CR to one graph edge and one name.

summary: realized the six frozen units as one new skill, four revised skills, one revised agent definition and a changeset

detail: impl gate round 1: 61 of 62 frozen scenarios passed; one failed. The shipped workflow collapsed the node's two empty-step-three branches into one rule, keeping only searched-and-found-nothing and dropping no-reachable-tracker, so a step that could not run stayed indistinguishable from one that ran empty - the exact state the node exists to make visible. Fixed by giving step three the three distinct entry forms its graph draws. Also carried three gaps the judge found outside the frozen set: the guard-companion tell lost its paired-against-the-whole-map scope in the agent and would have blocked a change request that added a guard whose companion already existed; the rewrite escape was disclosed in the spec but not in the agent; and the producer was pointed at an agent definition it cannot load by name for the tell set, now pointed at the bars that carry each tell.

impl gate round 3: all 62 frozen scenarios passed but the rollup failed on a structural blocker the scenarios structurally cannot see. The gate skill that actually performs the cold-judge spawn was untouched by this change request and instructed the spawner to pass the spec and feature only, so on the real gate path the relayed mode never arrives, the step-record tell reads as inapplicable, and an inapplicable tell is never reported - a silent pass of the mechanism this change request exists to install. Unlike the sibling declaration field, which degrades loudly because an empty set fails the subset check, this one degrades silently, so the change request converted a pre-existing prose inconsistency into a silent bypass. Root cause named by the judge and fixed at the rule rather than the instance: the dispatch channel had three participants and no canonical block, so every joint re-described it in prose and each re-description could drift. There is now one owned payload block, referenced by the gate rather than re-described. Also restored a pass-path mandate this change request had deleted while it was carrying two frozen scenarios, and bound three unbound mandates to observables.

impl gate round 4: 57 of 62, down from 62, with two structural blockers. Decisive fact for the loop: the canonical dispatch block I created last round precisely to fix this defect class at the rule shipped missing a field three of the four tells need - the baseline that what-the-change-request-added is computed against. The fix at the rule reproduced the defect it was written to eliminate. Multiple further findings name artifacts last round's remediation changed: the report block was not swept when the collect step gained a field, the report-each-miss mandate binds to an Output field that does not exist, the remediation gloss went to five keys against a canonical seven, and the pointer I repointed last round now resolves to a namespace that does not carry the content. Scenario count across four rounds: 61, 61, 62, 57.

why.blast: medium - the SDD self-spec's authoring and mission capabilities
why.novelty: medium - the re-plan that would actually work needs a mechanical reconciliation check, which is a new engine and a different change request, not a further edit to this one
why.confidence: low - three consecutive impl-gate rounds failed on one defect class, the last one through a fix aimed at that class's root cause, and the scenario count fell rather than rose

detail: impl gate round 5: 61 of 62, up from 57, with no structural blocker and no absorption finding. The round rebased onto the current target first, resolving one conflict in the root project spec, and then swept by hand the six open instances of the defect class the prior halt named, the mechanical check for it having been cut into its own change request. The judge independently re-derived all 62 oracles and confirmed all six corrections present and wired. The single failure: the canonical dispatch payload block states the step-record field is omitted on create/revise and never says what a conductor does when it invoked backfill mode and the producer returned no record at all, which is the case one frozen conductor scenario tests. The change request's own spec body for that node states the resolution correctly; the shipped skill a session actually loads does not carry it. Scenario count across five rounds: 61, 61, 62, 57, 61.

why.blast: medium - the SDD self-spec's authoring and mission capabilities
why.novelty: none - the round made no new design decision
why.confidence: low - the one failing finding names the canonical dispatch payload block, an artifact this round's own commit changed, which rule 4 reads as a regression regardless of whether this round introduced the gap. That block has now been the failing artifact two rounds running on two different completeness defects, which is the non-convergence signal the rule exists to catch. A sixth round would be a one-sentence patch to the artifact whose repeated incompleteness is the finding, which is the shape this change request was written to prevent
